deviations.qemu_behavior: Read from QEMU's hw/audio/hda-codec.c and hw/audio/intel-hda.c on master on 2026-10-23. QEMU's hda-duplex/hda-output codec moves output-stream DMA from a per-stream timer on QEMU_CLOCK_VIRTUAL that re-arms every 1 ms (HDA_TIMER_TICKS = SCALE_MS) and transfers the bytes the stream rate allows since the stream started; hda_timer_sync_adjust moves that start by 1 ms, or by 4 ms when far behind, to follow the audio backend's buffer level. The timer became the default in 2018 (commit bc753dc09f) and the only mode in 2025, when commit c2c8805742 removed the use-timer setting. Each transfer (intel_hda_xfer) walks the BDL, updates LPIB and an enabled DMA position buffer, sets BCIS when an entry flagged IOC completes and updates the controller interrupt, through MSI when the guest enabled it, else INTx. The pace therefore depends neither on vCPU exits nor on a host thread of the VMM.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: BridgeVM's HDA controller (crates/bridgevm-hvf/src/hda) advances playback and capture DMA by the host time elapsed since the previous poll of the controller, at most 100 ms per poll (longer gaps drop the excess). A poll runs in every vCPU drain, before CPU0 runs and after any vCPU's MMIO exit, and, from this change, in a host service tick every 5 ms while either stream's RUN is set (examples/hvf_gic_boot_probe/hda_service_tick.rs). The tick is deadline-paced at user-interactive QoS, takes the platform lock only with try_lock and skips a tick a vCPU or a reset holds, sends the MSI it takes after releasing the lock, never forces a vCPU exit, and is off under BRIDGEVM_USERSPACE_GIC, where exits alone poll as before. A completed IOC entry sets BCIS, and an MSI is sent only on a rising edge of the controller's interrupt level, so entries completed within one poll share one MSI. The function is MSI-only: it advertises no INTx pin. LPIB and an enabled position buffer advance in poll-sized steps.
deviations.impact: The guest sees DMA progress and IOC interrupts at the polls' granularity rather than QEMU's 1 ms timer cadence. Before this change that granularity was the guest's own exit pattern: T17 r92 recorded poll gaps up to 216 ms against Windows' 20 ms cyclic buffer, so audio the guest had not rewritten was played again, 116 ms was dropped, and 372 MSIs covered 568 IOCs. With the tick the expected gap is at most 5 ms plus the host's wake latency while the stream runs, and longer only while a vCPU holds the platform lock, when that vCPU's drain polls instead. Only deterministic tests at this change support that expectation; no live run has measured the guest-visible pacing.

deviations.qemu_behavior: Read from QEMU's hw/audio/intel-hda.c and hw/audio/hda-codec-common.h on master on 2026-11-04. intel-hda resets GCAP to 0x4401: four input stream descriptors (SD0-SD3 at 0x80-0xE0), then four output descriptors (SD4-SD7 at 0x100-0x160). hda-duplex (ID 1af4:0022 with mixer emulation, 1af4:0021 without) wires DAC 2 to a line-out jack, pin 3, and a line-in jack, pin 5, to ADC 4; hda-micro uses the same nodes with a speaker jack and a mic jack.
deviations.bridgevm_behavior: GCAP 0x1101: one input stream, SD0 at 0x80 (capture; LPIB alias 0x2084), and one output stream, SD1 at 0xA0 (playback; LPIB alias 0x20A4). Stream interrupt bits and DMA position entries follow that order. The codec keeps the 1af4:0022 ID and hda-duplex's node numbers, but pin 3 is a fixed internal speaker and pin 5 a fixed internal microphone. The ADC takes 16-bit 48 kHz PCM only and has no amp. Capture is paced like playback; it records the Mac's default input only when the VM's microphone setting is on and silence otherwise.
deviations.impact: Windows' HD Audio class driver shows one Speakers and one Microphone endpoint and applies its own capture volume and mute. A VM that booted an earlier build, whose codec had no input path, gains the Microphone endpoint at its first boot on this one; the playback endpoint keeps its codec ID and pin.
